memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "For the breastpiece make braided chains of pure gold, like a rope. Make two gold rings for it and fasten them to two corners of the breastpiece. Fasten the two gold chains to the rings at the corners of the breastpiece, and the other ends of the chains to the two settings, attaching them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front." - Exodus 28:22-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gives careful instructions for fastening the breastpiece. Rings, chains, settings, attachments — a whole system designed to hold it firmly in place. The breastpiece bearing the names of God's people was not going to swing loose or fall off. It was secured, deliberately and thoroughly.

Sometimes the most reassuring thing in Scripture is a detail about fastening. God does not do things loosely. The names of His people were held in place by design, connected at multiple points, tied to the shoulder pieces so that the weight was properly distributed and nothing could slip.

Jesus spoke about this kind of security when He said that no one can snatch His sheep out of His hand, and no one can snatch them out of the Father's hand (John 10:28-29). Two hands, multiple fastenings, nothing loose. Your place with God is not held by a single fragile thread that your worst day could snap. If you belong to Christ, you are securely fastened — not by the strength of your grip on Him, but by the strength of His grip on you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I rest in the security of God's grip, or fear that my hold might slip?
What anxiety about my standing with God can I hand over today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that my security rests on Your grip and not on mine. Quiet my fears about slipping away, and let me rest in how firmly You hold me in Christ. Amen.
